channel.title: Aera field notes
channel.description: What consumer wearables can and cannot measure, with the research behind each claim.

item.title: Why does my recovery app say I'm fit when I'm sick in bed?
item.description: Overnight signals are not a clean bill of health; the opposite mismatch also happens.

item.title: What is a repeated running route?
item.description: The same whole run you return to often enough that an app can name the ground, count returns, and time it with fixed gates.

item.title: What are running segments?
item.description: Repeated stretches your runs keep covering, found and timed with gates. No leaderboard. The only person on the course is you.

item.title: How long will this climb take me?
item.description: Read remaining ground in minutes from your recent pace, after correcting each stretch for how much climb costs. About, not a promise.

item.title: When should I start a training plan?
item.description: When your own week already shows a steady rhythm. A plan shapes a habit you have.

item.title: Should I sometimes push harder on an easy day?
item.description: Sometimes, on a settled day. A small optional stretch builds the ceiling. A daily push does not.

item.title: How long will this route take me?
item.description: A range from your own comparable workouts, not a map app travel time.

item.title: What can a consumer watch not measure?
item.description: Heart and movement from the wrist are strong. Blood chemistry, genes, and most illness are not.

item.title: Why should a watch compare me to myself?
item.description: People differ too much for group averages. Your own recent weeks are the meaningful band.

item.title: Should I make up a missed workout?
item.description: Usually no. Leave the miss alone. Stacking catch-up kilometres is how weekly distance jumps.

item.title: Why does biological age move slowly?
item.description: Watch aging reads follow weeks of habit, not one night or one workout.

item.title: How should I read heart-rate recovery?
item.description: Compare the first-minute drop only under matched efforts. Trend beats one number.

item.title: What is biological age?
item.description: A wearable estimate of how recent heart, fitness, and sleep signals compare with peers, not a second birthday.

item.title: How will training affect tomorrow's recovery?
item.description: Easy work usually clears by morning. Hard work more often leaves a quieter read. Neither is a forecast.

item.title: What does a training streak mean?
item.description: Weeks you showed up with at least one recorded session. A count of attendance, not a fitness grade.

item.title: Why does heat raise my heart rate?
item.description: On a warm or humid day your heart runs higher at the same pace. That is weather working, not lost fitness.

item.title: What are personal record distances?
item.description: The fastest stretch of an exact distance inside a run, tracked at five common marks. GPS noise is worse on short ones.

item.title: What is a recent best versus a personal record?
item.description: Same stopwatch, two windows. Neither one is a race forecast.

item.title: Does exercise help you sleep deeper tonight?
item.description: Direction, not dose. A session can nudge slow-wave sleep; hard or late can go the other way.

item.title: What are running splits?
item.description: Equal pieces of a run that show whether pace held, drifted, or faded. A shape, not a grade.
